name: Question 9
problem: A particle $P$ of mass $6\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis from rest at the origin with an acceleration of magnitude $(1+{t}^{2})\,{m/s}^{2},$ where the acceleration acts in the direction of increasing $x,$ and $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the particle's kinetic energy at time $t=1\,s.$
worked_solution:
The kinetic energy of a particle with mass $m$ and velocity $v$ is given by

$$
\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}.
$$

When the mass and velocity are measured in kilograms and meters per second, respectively, the particle's kinetic energy is measured in Joules ($J$).

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =\int (1+{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =t+\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
0=0+\frac{1}{3}({0}^{3})+C\,⟹\,C=0.
$$

Hence, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=t+\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}.$ In particular, its velocity at time $t=1\,s$ is

$$
v=v(1)=1+\frac{1}{3}({1}^{3})=\frac{4}{3}\,m/s.
$$

Therefore, the kinetic energy of the particle at $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{KE} & =\frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot \frac{16}{9} \\  & =\frac{16}{3}\,J.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

A particle P of mass 6kg moves along the x-axis from rest at the origin with an acceleration of magnitude (1+t2)m/s2, where the acceleration acts in the direction of increasing x, and t≥0 is the time in seconds. Calculate the particle's kinetic energy at time t=1s.

a
112J
b
163J
c
152J
d
76J
e
83J
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The kinetic energy of a particle with mass m and velocity v is given by KE=12mv2.

When the mass and velocity are measured in kilograms and meters per second, respectively, the particle's kinetic energy is measured in Joules (J).

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time: v(t)=∫a(t)dtv(t)=∫(1+t2)dtv(t)=t+13t3+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=0. Substituting this into the above gives 0=0+13(03)+C⟹C=0.

Hence, the velocity of the particle at time t is v(t)=t+13t3. In particular, its velocity at time t=1s is v=v(1)=1+13(13)=43m/s.

Therefore, the kinetic energy of the particle at t=1 is KE=12mv2=12⋅6⋅(43)2=12⋅6⋅169=163J.
